# Development Journal

## Software Stack

- **Language:** Kotlin
- **UI:** Jetpack Compose (Material3), Compose BOM 2026.06.01 (Compose 1.11.4, Material 3 1.4.0, material-icons-core 1.7.8)
- **Min SDK:** 34 (Android 14)
- **Target/Compile SDK:** 36
- **Location:** platform `LocationManager` + `GPS_PROVIDER` (no Play Services / FusedLocationProvider); optional external classic-Bluetooth GNSS receiver over SPP/NMEA
- **Persistence:** per-run append-only fixed-size binary files + `SharedPreferences` (no Room, no DataStore)
- **State sharing:** `Application`-scoped singleton + `StateFlow` (no DI framework)
- **Build:** CI-only via GitHub Actions (Gradle 9.4.0, AGP 9.1.0, Kotlin Compose plugin 2.3.10, JDK 17)

## Key Decisions

**AGP 9's built-in Kotlin support is used; no separate `kotlin-android` plugin.**
AGP 9.1 registers the `compileDebugKotlin` task and the `kotlin { }` extension on its own, so only `com.android.application` and the Compose compiler plugin are applied.

**The Compose BOM is the newest one that compiles against SDK 36; lifecycle 2.10 for the same reason.**
Compose 1.12 (BOM 2026.08.00 and later) and lifecycle 2.11 declare `minCompileSdk=37`, and AGP 9.1.0's maximum compile SDK is 36, so the September 2026 BOM broke every CI job at the AAR-metadata check. BOM 2026.06.01 (Compose 1.11.4; Material 3 stays 1.4.0, so the UI code is unaffected) and lifecycle 2.10.0 are the last releases with `minCompileSdk=35`. Moving past them is a toolchain task — AGP 9.4+, compileSdk/targetSdk 37 and the matching Kotlin/Compose-compiler plugin — that has to be verified in CI on its own, not folded into a UI change. `material-icons-core` is declared explicitly: material3 depends on it only at runtime, so `Icons.*` does not resolve without it.

**Non-Compose AndroidX dependencies carry explicit versions.**
`androidx.compose:compose-bom` only constrains the `androidx.compose.*` groups. `androidx.activity:activity-compose` is pinned explicitly.

**Release signing comes from environment variables, not a properties file.**
`SIGNING_KEYSTORE_PATH`, `SIGNING_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `SIGNING_KEY_ALIAS` and `SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD` are read in `app/build.gradle.kts`. The keystore never enters the repository, and when the variables are absent the signing config is simply not created, so debug builds and local release builds still work.

**Version metadata is a Gradle property, sourced from the release tag.**
The release workflow resolves the tag, derives `versionCode` as `major * 10000 + minor * 100 + patch`, and passes both via `-P` flags.

**Every push to `main` publishes a signed `dev` pre-release.**
`build.yml` runs lint and unit tests, then builds a *signed release* APK (`versionName = dev-<short-sha>`) and publishes it as a single rolling `dev` GitHub pre-release, deleting and recreating it each run so there is always exactly one current dev artifact. Signing is real (env-var driven), so the pre-release depends on the `SIGNING_*` secrets being present. Modelled on `c0dev0id/androsnd`; the `andro-template` workflow it was originally scaffolded from is outdated. `release.yml` (manual `workflow_dispatch` → tagged draft release) is kept separate and is not the day-to-day path.

**minSdk raised to 34 to delete all compatibility code.**
At API 34 the runtime `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` permission, `FOREGROUND_SERVICE_LOCATION`, the 3-arg `startForeground`, and the `LocationManager` `Executor`/`Looper` overloads are all unconditionally available, so no `androidx.core` compat layer or version guards are needed. Android 13 and older are unsupported by design.

**`LocationManager` + `GPS_PROVIDER`, not FusedLocationProvider.**
FusedLocationProvider is a Play Services dependency, caps at roughly 1 Hz and smooths fixes. Raw chipset-rate logging (device-dependent, up to ~10–20 Hz) requires `requestLocationUpdates(minTime=0, minDistance=0)` on the platform provider. Fixes are delivered on a dedicated `HandlerThread`, never the main Looper.

**Launcher icon is vector-only, no PNG density buckets.**
`mipmap-anydpi/ic_launcher.xml` is an adaptive icon whose background (gradient), foreground and monochrome layers are all `VectorDrawable`s under `res/drawable/`. With minSdk 34 every device supports adaptive icons, so no legacy `mipmap-*dpi` PNGs exist and the folder carries no `-v26` qualifier. The notification small icon `ic_stat_logging` is the same path data cropped to the 66dp safe zone. The SVG source of truth is the path data itself; regenerate previews by rendering the drawables' `pathData` in an SVG.

**A missing GNSS chipset is a supported configuration, not a crash.**
`requestLocationUpdates` throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a provider that does not exist, and a device with no GNSS hardware (a Wi-Fi-only tablet) has no `GPS_PROVIDER` at all. The call sits on the `gps-logger` HandlerThread and only `SecurityException` was caught, so starting a run there killed the process. `LocationManager.hasProvider` (API 31) is the platform's own presence question and is asked in exactly two places: `LoggingService.startSource` refuses the internal source, which routes into the existing "could not acquire the source" path so no empty run file and no zombie service is left behind; and `MainViewModel.hasInternalGps` reads it once for the UI — a `val`, not a `StateFlow`, because hardware cannot appear while the process lives. `isProviderEnabled` is only *specified* for a provider that exists (the current implementation happens to answer false, but the contract does not say so), so both of its call sites go through one `internalGpsEnabled()` helper that asks presence first. `RecordStatus.NoDevice` ranks above `Unavailable` because a missing chipset is not something a permission grant fixes, and it applies only while idle — a run already recording reports what it is doing. The Start button's enabled state became `status == RecordStatus.Idle`: one predicate for both, so the headline word and the button can never contradict each other. The manifest's `uses-feature android.hardware.location.gps` moved to `required="false"`, because a run can come from an external Bluetooth NMEA receiver and internal GNSS was therefore never a requirement.

**Precise (fine) location is mandatory and checked explicitly.**
Since Android 12 a coarse-only app may still request `GPS_PROVIDER`; nothing throws, but fixes are fuzzed and throttled to one per 10 minutes and `GnssStatus` callbacks register yet never fire. That presents as a run with no points and "Receiver off". The Activity checks `ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION` on resume and surfaces a banner, and `LoggingService.startLogging` refuses to start without it, so the failure is named instead of silent.

**Fix status comes from `GnssStatus`, not from fix age.**
A `GnssStatus.Callback` is registered next to the location updates (same handler thread, ~1 Hz from the engine). "Has fix" is defined as at least one satellite flagged `usedInFix`; this is the platform's own notion, updates even while no `Location` arrives, and needs no timer to expire a stale fix. Provider on/off is taken from `LocationListener.onProviderEnabled/Disabled`. The per-fix state update copies the existing `LoggingState` so these fields survive.

**One append-only fixed-size binary file per run, not a database.**
Each run is `filesDir/runs/<startMillis>.dat`: a 16-byte header plus 68-byte records with a validity bitmask (absent optional fields written as NaN sentinels). Point count is `(size − header) / recordSize` in O(1); a torn trailing partial record is ignored for crash safety. No end marker — a graceful stop and a crash are indistinguishable, and interrupted runs are just runs. This honours the pre-1.0 "no schema/migration code" rule.

**In-memory buffer flushed (no fsync) every 60 s; no wake lock held.**
Records accumulate in memory and are written to the OS page cache on the flush cadence. `fdatasync()` was dropped — only a power-loss crash can lose data, which is acceptable for this use case. The `PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK` was also dropped: the foreground-service type `LOCATION` combined with the GPS hardware keeps the relevant subsystems running; holding a CPU wake lock for a multi-hour run burns unnecessary heat. A power-loss crash loses at most one flush interval of points; a process kill is handled by the OS page cache surviving.

**Auto-resume via persisted active-run flag + START_STICKY + BOOT_COMPLETED.**
The active run id is written to `SharedPreferences` on start and cleared on stop. A system-driven restart (`START_STICKY`, null intent) and a reboot (`BootReceiver`) both re-open the same file in append mode and keep logging until the user taps Stop. A battery-optimization exemption is requested so the OS leaves the service alone; both the exemption and receiving `BOOT_COMPLETED` are background-FGS-start exemptions (OEM aggressiveness still varies). A user-initiated Force-Stop is a permanent OS stop and is not resumed, by design.

**Export filters: accuracy first, then distance/time with "distance beats time".**
Accuracy always drops missing/worse fixes. When distance > 0 the decision is governed entirely by distance (minimum spacing from the last kept point); time only governs cadence when distance is 0. Both off keeps all accuracy-passing points. `PointFilter` and `RunCodec` are pure Kotlin so they are unit-tested on the JVM in CI — they carry the highest on-paper risk.

**GPX written with the built-in `android.util.Xml` serializer, streamed to the output.**
No XML library. One `<trk>` per run; a new `<trkseg>` is started across gaps larger than 60 s (e.g. a reboot pause) so viewers don't draw a straight line over the gap.

**UI is four surfaces behind a bottom `NavigationBar`, not tabs (supersedes "four tabs").**
The first cut put every control and the runs list in a single `LazyColumn`; live stats then reflowed the list on start/stop and in landscape pushed it off-screen, and the whole thing scrolled as one blob. Splitting into **Record**, **Runs**, **Export** and **Settings** gave each surface its own scroll; that split stays. What changed in the polish redesign is the container: four unrelated top-level destinations are what Material 3's navigation bar is for (tabs are for sibling views inside one destination), `NavigationBarItem(enabled = false)` gives the Export gating a real disabled state instead of a 0.38-alpha label hack, `BadgedBox`/`Badge` carry the recording dot (error while recording, the neutral `outline` while paused, with a content description — dynamic tertiary is the primary hue + 60°, which lands on red for pink and magenta wallpapers and would have made paused and recording identical in the one place with no word next to the dot; the words use `onSurfaceVariant`) and the selection count (replacing the "Export (N)" label), and an 80 dp bar is under the thumb. The permanent `TopAppBar` is gone — a "gpsLog" title cost 64 dp on every surface and carried no information; Runs, Export and Settings start with a 56 dp `SurfaceHeader`, Record's status hero is its header. Everything the tabs decision protected is unchanged: one Compose screen, a `rememberSaveable` index and a `when`, no `navigation-compose`, the `LaunchedEffect` fallback from Export to Runs when the selection is empty. The shell now collects only `activeRun` and `selected`; each surface lives in its own file and collects its own flows, so a 2 s `LoggingState` tick recomposes `RecordSurface` alone (`ActiveRun(id, paused)` is a `distinct` reduction of the state, so the bar and the Runs list never see point ticks).

**Wide windows get a navigation rail and two-column surfaces; the boundary is 600 dp, read from the window itself.**
On a tablet or a phone in landscape the bottom bar cost 80 dp of an already short height, the 600 dp content column left wide empty margins, and the Record tiles were cut off below the fold. Material's own answer is the compact/medium boundary: at 600 dp and above the `NavigationBar` becomes a `NavigationRail` on the start side (same four destinations, same badges, built from one `destinations` list so the two never drift), and Record puts its status and controls beside the tile panel while Export puts the filters beside the result, both capped at 840 dp. The width comes from `LocalWindowInfo.current.containerDpSize` — a stable Compose API that recomposes on rotation — so no `material3-window-size-class` or `androidx.window` dependency is needed for one threshold. Runs and Settings stay single 600 dp columns, which is what Material wants for lists.

A first cut of that split kept both columns at their natural height at the top of the window, which on a landscape phone left the bottom half empty and made the short status column look unrelated to the taller tile panel. While a run is recording, both columns are now given the window's height as a minimum — capped by `WideContentMaxHeight` (560 dp) so a tall window (a tablet either way up, where `wide` is also true) stops stretching — the status block centres inside its column, the six tiles share the panel with `SpaceEvenly`, and their numerals take the next type step (`headlineMedium`). Idle content is not stretched: a hero plus the latest-run row keeps its natural height and is centred. The minimum height is applied to the `Column` inside `Panel` rather than to the panel itself: material3 1.4.0's `Surface` does not route through `Box(propagateMinConstraints = true)`, so a minimum constraint on the panel is not guaranteed to reach its content, whereas content that is genuinely tall always grows the `Surface` around it. The window height comes from `BoxWithConstraints`, which is the only way to know the content area (the navigation rail and the system bars have already been subtracted at that point) — `LocalWindowInfo` would report the whole window.

**Export is a verb, not a place (supersedes the Export gating, badge and fallback described above).**
Material's navigation bar holds top-level places of equal standing that are always reachable; an action on chosen content is a contextual action, and a child of a destination is a pushed screen with Back. The disabled Export destination violated both, and every oddity followed from it: the count badge (a destination pretending to be a verb), the `LaunchedEffect` fallback (a place that could stop existing), the permanent checkbox on every row (selection had to be the row's only tap because the verb lived elsewhere) and the dead end after Stop. Now `MainViewModel.exportTarget: Set<Long>` names the runs the Export page is open for — empty means closed, one value with no invariant to maintain — kept apart from the Runs selection so a tap on one run or on the latest run from Record opens its page without disturbing a selection, and Back returns to it intact. The page is composed in the shell's content slot while the subject is non-empty; Back (`BackHandler` from activity-compose), the page's arrow and every navigation item close it (`closeExport()` before switching). The subject lives in the ViewModel, not `rememberSaveable`, on purpose: it survives rotation with a half-edited filter and dies with the process so no saved index can outlive its content — do not "fix" it into a saveable flag plus a repair effect. The earlier bottom sheet is not brought back: `ModalBottomSheet` is still `@ExperimentalMaterial3Api` in material3 1.4.0 (the UI carries no opt-in) and three IME fields plus a preview do not fit a half sheet. The export filters act only on this page — recording always logs every raw fix. Share GPX is never disabled: `export()` filters the points itself and never reads the preview, and the panel already names an empty result. Core loop: Stop → Latest run → Share GPX, 3 taps where it was 5.

**Record's idle slot is the latest run, not six dashes.**
The "nothing jumps on Start" rationale protected the button under the finger; the controls sit above the slot in both layouts, so the slot's content may change under the user's own tap. Six tiles reading "—" under a status word that already says "Ready" carried no information; the run just recorded, with a Share glyph, is the on-ramp the flow lacked. The row reads `runs.firstOrNull()` — no new state; the active run is listed at Start, so the id is right from the first frame after Stop, and the `runId` flip's `refreshRuns()` brings the duration and count up to date after one IO listing. With no runs the slot is empty (the Runs empty state already says "Press Start").

**Runs uses the platform selection idiom (supersedes "Row actions" above).**
A tap opens the run's Export page, a long-press selects it and starts selection mode (checkboxes appear, the header becomes a count with Close, Back leaves the mode), and the tray acts on the selection with Delete, Merge and Export. Argued against the recorded rationale: the checkbox was introduced because swipe-right selection had no affordance — true of a hidden swipe, but long-press is the convention of Files, Photos and Messages, TalkBack reads it from the long-click label, and a single-run export needs no selection at all; a list that looked like a form all the time was the price of the disabled destination. Swipe-to-delete stays out (a per-row verb next to a multiselection; an unconfirmed swipe needs a pending-delete mode). Implementation rule: ONE `combinedClickable` in both modes whose lambdas branch on `selecting`, with `onLongClick` always non-null — never swap `toggleable` for `combinedClickable` inside a `LazyColumn` row, because the swap happens while the finger is still down. Merge keeps the merged run selected (`repo.merge` already returned its id): merge-then-export is the reason to merge. Known risk: nothing on the idle list says "long-press to select"; the fallback, deliberately not shipped, is a "Select" text button in the Runs header backed by one `rememberSaveable` Boolean.

**Stop is a notification action, after Pause/Resume, unconfirmed.**
Same rationale as the unconfirmed in-app Stop (a mis-tap loses nothing; Start + Merge rejoin the halves and the 60 s gap rule draws a new segment), and it closes the hole the pause entry names: a run that comes back paused after a reboot could only be ended by opening the app. The toggle slot stays first so it never moves under the finger; request codes are `action.hashCode()`, so the three intents are distinct.

**Visual calibration pass: one scale, bounded rows, nothing dominating.**
Seen on a real tablet the redesign had four faults, all of them mine. (1) The type spanned the whole Material scale on one screen, 12 sp labels against a 36 sp status word, because each element was sized for its own importance rather than against a common step; the range is now roughly two, `headlineLarge` down to `labelLarge`. (2) The navigation rail was the phone's compact rail dropped unchanged onto a tablet, so it read as an afterthought beside inflated content; its glyph and label take one step up. `WideNavigationRail` is available and carries no experimental opt-in in material3 1.4.0, but expanded it costs about 220 dp of width, which a landscape phone at the 600 dp threshold cannot spare, and collapsed it gains 16 dp, so enlarging the contents of the stable rail was the better trade. (3) The run rows had a transparent container, no divider and no control, so at the width of a wide window a short date left nothing marking the row and nothing saying a tap exports it: they now carry a divider and a trailing Share glyph, and the active-run tag moved to the overline, where it is beside its run instead of stranded at the far edge. (4) Filling the panel's height with `SpaceEvenly` put more space between the tile rows than the rows occupied, so six values read as three floating pairs; a fixed `TileGap`, centred, fills the same space without the rows losing each other. Stop also lost its filled error container for an outline with error content, matching Delete on the Runs tray: a solid red block was the heaviest thing on a screen reporting that everything is fine, on the button pressed least.

**The GPS device picker is collapsed behind a row, because the list is unbounded.**
The inline `selectableGroup` list was the right call against a dropdown and against an experimental bottom sheet, but it ignored length: Bluetooth Class-of-Device carries no GNSS flag, so every paired classic device is offered, and a phone with twenty of them pushed Diagnostics and About off the screen. Settings now shows one row naming the current source and opens an `AlertDialog` with the same radio rows, scrollable, with the lazy `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` grant inside it. The rows in the dialog are plain `Row`s rather than `ListItem`s: a list item paints its own surface colour and would band against the dialog's container. It stays first in Settings rather than being demoted, because comparing the internal chipset against an external receiver is the reason the feature exists, so the source is switched often rather than once.

**Record is a status hero over one tile panel; the status comes from a pure, source-aware helper.**
The label/value rows became a `displaySmall` status word (Ready, Unavailable, Searching, Fix, Paused, Receiver off, GPS disabled) coloured by state, a subtitle, 56 dp text-only controls and six `headlineSmall` tiles in one `surfaceContainerLow` panel (fixed `Row`s, not `FlowRow`, so a tick costs no measurement pass; leaf composables take Strings and skip unless their text changed). The subtitle's recorded span is `lastFixTimeMillis − startTimeMillis`, which advances with fixes and freezes while paused — an elapsed-time clock was rejected because it needs 1 Hz recomposition while the state moves every 2 s. Speed stays in m/s, the file's unit. Recording is independent of the export filters — the service logs every raw fix and the filters act only at export time — so nothing on Record reads them; an early cross-link that flagged a fix worse than the export accuracy limit was dropped for exactly that reason. Controls: Stop left in `errorContainer` (a mis-tap loses nothing — Merge rejoins the runs), Pause/Resume right under the thumb, one filled-primary button at a time and it is always the "make it record" verb; Stop/Pause are text, not glyphs — `material-icons-core` has no pause/stop icon and neither a hand-drawn `ImageVector` nor `material-icons-extended` was worth it. `recordStatus(state, external, preciseLocation)` fixed a real mislabel: `LoggingService` initialises `gpsEnabled = isInternalSource() && …` and drops it on a Bluetooth disconnect, so the old `!gpsEnabled → "Disabled"` branch called a connecting or reconnecting external receiver "GPS disabled"; the helper maps that case to *Receiver off* and only the internal source to *GPS disabled*. The precedence table is unit-tested.

**Formatting is pure Kotlin under JUnit; leaf composables receive Strings.**
`ui/Format.kt` holds `Formats(locale, zone)` (locale-aware `NumberFormat`/`DateTimeFormatter`, built once and remembered per surface), `formatDuration`, `reductionPercent` (rounded, not floored) and the filter parsers `parseIntIn`/`parseDistance` (comma accepted, 0.1 rounding); `ui/RecordStatus.kt` holds the status and subtitle derivation. Both have no Android imports and are covered by `FormatTest`/`RecordStatusTest`. Run titles are absolute dates ("12 Sep 2026, 08:14") — deterministic, no remembered clock, no midnight staleness. `Formats` is never passed below surface level, so its stability never affects skipping.

**Settings is list rows with an inline radio list for the GPS device.**
The read-only `ExposedDropdownMenuBox` text field (a false input affordance and the UI's last experimental Material opt-in) became a `selectableGroup` of `ListItem` + `RadioButton` rows, so the choice and its alternatives are visible at once; the lazy `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` grant is an "Allow" row that the device rows replace in place. The updater is one `ListItem` whose slots follow `UpdateState`. "Share latest log" was a silent no-op with no log; it is now disabled with "No log captured yet", backed by `MainViewModel.latestDebugLog`, a `StateFlow` refreshed on IO inside `refreshRuns()` — which already runs on resume and on every `runId` flip, exactly when a log can appear — instead of a main-thread directory listing at composition.

**Theme: stable `MaterialTheme`, tabular numerals on the numeric roles, a dark launch theme, a fixed motion budget.**
`MaterialExpressiveTheme` was rejected: an experimental opt-in at the theme root for spring motion a still recording screen does not want (and material3 1.4.0 keeps the `MotionScheme` factories internal anyway). `tnum` is applied to display/headline/title only, so prose in body/label roles keeps proportional figures; the filter fields set it locally. `res/values-night/themes.xml` gives `Theme.App` the dark `Material.NoActionBar` parent so the first frame is dark. Motion is exactly two `AnimatedVisibility` transitions (precise-location banner, selection tray) plus what components animate themselves; no pulsing recording dot (an infinite animation would hold the frame clock for the whole run to redraw a dot that is already visible — the climbing point count is the liveness signal), no crossfade on the status word, no destination transitions, no number tweening.

**Row actions: checkbox multiselect; Delete and Merge act on the whole selection; Delete confirms.**
Selection is a leading `Checkbox` and the whole row (a stock two-line `ListItem`, `toggleable` with `Role.Checkbox`, tinted `secondaryContainer` when selected) toggles it. The earlier swipe-to-reveal delete was dropped entirely: having multiselect but only being able to action one row at a time (per-row swipe) was inconsistent, so Delete — and Merge — are buttons in an `ActionTray` below the list that operate on the multiselection. The active run may be selected for export but is excluded from Delete/Merge (its file is being appended); the buttons' counts and enabled state reflect the selection minus the active run (Delete needs ≥1, Merge ≥2). Delete now asks through an `AlertDialog` because it is the app's one irreversible action; Merge does not (points in, points out). A header "Clear" (`clearSelection()`) drops a multi-row selection, since with Export gated on the selection there was otherwise no way but tapping every row.

**Merge rewrites the selected runs into one file via the normal codec.**
`RunRepository.merge` reads every selected run with `RunReader.readAll`, concatenates the points, sorts them by time, and writes a single run with `RunWriter` (same header/record codec as live logging). It writes to a `.dat.tmp` first, then deletes the originals and renames the temp over the earliest run's id, so a crash mid-merge leaves the originals intact. The merged run's id is `min(ids)` (the earliest start). Honours the pre-1.0 "no schema/migration" rule — it's just points in, points out.

**Export is its own surface with a live filtered-result preview, tied to the selection.**
The always-visible filter fields, the bottom sheet and the separate Save/Share buttons are gone. Selecting runs enables the **Export** destination (its navigation item carries the count as a badge) which shows a summary of the selection (run count + raw point total from `RunInfo.pointCount`, free), the accuracy/distance/time filters, a live **Result** panel (kept points as a numeral, plus the total, the track count and the percentage reduction) and a single **Export GPX** action. The Save-file (SAF `CreateDocument`) path was dropped because sharing the GPX to a file manager already writes it to disk — one Share action suffices. The result preview is a `StateFlow<ExportPreview>` on the ViewModel built with `combine(selected, filters, runs)` → `transformLatest` (`@ExperimentalCoroutinesApi`), so a filter change mid-read cancels the stale computation; each recompute reads every selected run via `RunReader.readAll` and runs `PointFilter` on `Dispatchers.IO`, emitting `Computing` then `Ready`. It re-reads files on each change (no retained point cache) — KISS over memory-heavy caching, acceptable because reads are fast and cancellation-friendly. The Export button is disabled until the preview is `Ready`; while `Computing` the panel keeps the last `Ready` figures dimmed rather than flashing a placeholder. Filters are rows (meaning left, a 120 dp field with the unit as a `suffix` right): a valid entry commits immediately, an invalid one flags the field with the range and snaps back to the persisted value on focus loss, so the field never shows a number that is not in effect. Time stays enabled while a distance is set — its helper states PointFilter's distance-beats-time rule — because a user may set time first and clear distance after. The root has `imePadding()`, and the shell consumes the Scaffold padding as insets so that padding measures from the navigation bar rather than a bar's height above the keyboard.

**Dynamic (Material You) colour via a `GpsLogTheme` wrapper.**
The app previously used a bare `MaterialTheme {}` with no `colorScheme`, i.e. the baseline purple and no dark mode. `ui/Theme.kt` selects `dynamicLightColorScheme`/`dynamicDarkColorScheme` from `isSystemInDarkTheme()`; at minSdk 34 both are unconditionally available, so no fallback palette and no version guard. Colour roles are used consistently: `onSurfaceVariant` for every label and helper (the earlier `outline`-as-text failed contrast in dark mode), `surfaceContainerLow` for panels, `surfaceContainer` for the bar and trays, `errorContainer` for the standing Stop button and the precise-location banner, full `error` only for the confirming Delete.

**In-app nightly updater talks to the GitHub releases API, no token, no library.**
The Settings tab has a "Check for updates" control. `UpdateChecker` does a plain `HttpURLConnection` GET of `releases/tags/dev` (the rolling pre-release) and parses it with the built-in `org.json` — release assets on a public repo download anonymously, so no token is embedded, and a `User-Agent` header is set because GitHub 403s requests without one. The asset is `gpslog-dev-<sha>.apk` and the installed `versionName` is `dev-<sha>`, so "new" is decided by comparing the short SHA. Note this can only detect *different*, not *newer* — dev SHAs are unordered and no build timestamp is stored. The APK is streamed to `cacheDir/downloads/` and handed to the system installer via `ACTION_VIEW` + `FileProvider`. This needs `REQUEST_INSTALL_PACKAGES` (banned on Play, fine for GitHub distribution) and `INTERNET` (the app's first use of the network — location logging never needed it); the first install routes the user through `ACTION_MANAGE_UNKNOWN_APP_SOURCES`. Crucially, an in-place update only succeeds when the nightly is signed with the same key as the installed build (the CI keystore) — a differently-signed or local build must be uninstalled first.

**Recording source is pluggable: internal GPS or an external classic-Bluetooth NMEA receiver.**
The motivation is comparison — recording an external receiver while the phone's own GPS stays free for navigation. A `FixSink` interface (`onFix`/`onSatelliteStatus`/`onSourceEnabled`) is the seam both sources drive; `LoggingService` implements it and `startLogging` branches on `SettingsStore.recordingSource` (`""` = internal, otherwise a paired MAC). The internal path is unchanged. The external path is `BluetoothNmeaSource`: an RFCOMM socket on the SPP UUID `00001101-0000-1000-8000-00805F9B34FB`, read on its **own** thread (a blocking socket read must not sit on the `gps-logger` HandlerThread and starve the flush/notification callbacks), with each parsed fix `handler.post`ed back onto the logger thread so the writer and its counters stay single-threaded. It auto-reconnects on drop and reports the receiver off in the meantime. Classic Bluetooth (SPP), not BLE — it's a plain ASCII byte stream, simpler than GATT.

**Bluetooth devices are not filtered for "is this a GNSS device"; the user picks.**
Bluetooth Class-of-Device has no GNSS class and SPP receivers report as uncategorized, so there is no reliable programmatic signal. The Settings picker lists every paired classic/dual device by name and trusts the user's choice. `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` is requested lazily from the picker (via a Compose `rememberLauncherForActivityResult`), never in the up-front location chain, so an internal-only user is never prompted. No `BLUETOOTH_SCAN` — only bonded devices are read, never discovery.

**UI state updates suppressed in background; all updates throttled to 2 s.**
`LoggingStateHolder` carries a `@Volatile uiVisible` flag flipped by `MainActivity.onResume/onPause`. When the app is in background, `LoggingService` skips the per-fix and satellite-status `StateFlow` updates entirely — no allocations, no Compose recompositions. The notification update (always visible) is unconditional. When in foreground, updates are throttled to 2 s (previously 250 ms / 1 s) — adequate for a stats display, and the single biggest recomposition savings at the internal 1 Hz / external 4 Hz fix rate. Satellite status posts from `BluetoothNmeaSource` are additionally time-gated to 2 s: the incremental GSV accumulation (3 talkers × 4 Hz = ~12 posts/sec) was the most wasteful path.

**NMEA parsing is `GGA` + `RMC` only; `GSA`/`GSV` are optional enrichment.**
`data/NmeaParser` is pure Kotlin (unit-tested in CI like `PointFilter`/`RunCodec`), talker-agnostic (accepts `GP`/`GN`/`GL`/… by matching the 3-char sentence type). RMC carries the only date, so it is the emit trigger; a `GpsRecord` is produced per valid RMC (status `A`), enriched with the most recent GGA (MSL altitude, HDOP, fix quality, satellites-in-use). NMEA has no meters-accuracy field and `PointFilter` drops points with missing accuracy, so accuracy is derived as `HDOP × 5 m` (nominal UERE) — otherwise every external point would be filtered out on export. GSV, if present, sums satellites-in-view across per-constellation talkers purely for the live stats. Reference device: a GNS 3000 (MediaTek MT3333, SBAS-capable — its DGPS/SBAS fixes report GGA quality 2, which the parser accepts as any quality > 0).

**Raw-NMEA capture is a passive tee to a shareable file, not a device query.**
Over SPP a NMEA receiver only *streams*; it cannot be "queried" for capabilities like a REST API (that would need vendor `PMTK` commands written back to the device — deliberately out of scope for now). But the stream itself reveals the config: active constellations from the GSV talker IDs, delivery rate from line timestamps, HDOP and fix quality from GGA. So a Settings toggle (`SettingsStore.debugLogging`) makes `BluetoothNmeaSource` tee each raw line to `cacheDir/debug/nmea-<runId>.log` via `NmeaDebugLog`, timestamped `HH:mm:ss.SSS`. All file IO stays on the reader thread (opened at the top of `runLoop`, closed in its `finally`), so the single-threaded writer contract is untouched. The file is shared through the existing `FileProvider` (`text/plain`), and `MainViewModel.latestDebugLog()` picks the newest file in the debug dir. Motivation: diagnose why an external receiver (GNS 3000 / MT3333) reports fewer satellites and lower accuracy than the tablet's internal chipset — likely fewer enabled constellations and single-frequency silicon, with the HDOP×5 accuracy heuristic possibly tripping the 10 m export filter.

The internal GPS gets the same treatment so the two sources can be compared on equal footing. The internal chipset emits no NMEA of its own accessible over `LocationManager`, but the platform exposes an NMEA stream via `addNmeaListener(Executor, OnNmeaMessageListener)` — registered on the same `handlerExecutor` that marshals the `GnssStatus` callback, so `NmeaDebugLog.line()` stays on the `gps-logger` thread. Before streaming, the log also records `getGnssHardwareModelName()`, `getGnssYearOfHardware()` and `getGnssCapabilities()` — a static probe of what the silicon *can* do (measurements, multi-constellation, dual-frequency) versus what it currently emits. This is the cheap data-gathering step behind the user's "direct internal option" idea: the 1 Hz cap has no app-level knob (`requestLocationUpdates` already runs `minTime=0`), so before building anything we want to see whether the capabilities suggest any headroom at all.

**Pause is a cold state: the fix source is released, and the state is persisted.**
Pause originally set a flag that made `onFix` drop records while the `LocationListener`, the `GnssStatus` callback and the RFCOMM socket all stayed live. Since the GPS chipset is by far the dominant drain, a paused run cost very nearly as much as a recording one — the feature did not do the one thing its name promises. `startLogging`'s source setup and the teardown duplicated in `stopLoggingInternal`/`onDestroy` were factored out as `startSource()`/`stopSource()`, so pause now releases the source outright, flushes the writer and cancels the flush timer; the chipset powers down and the run costs nothing until Resume re-acquires it (a warm start, since the ephemeris is still cached). There is no wake lock to release — that was already dropped earlier.

The paused flag is persisted next to the active run id, which also fixed a real bug: `BootReceiver` and the `START_STICKY` null-intent path both funnel into `startLogging`, which hardcoded `paused = false`, so a reboot or a process kill while paused silently resumed *recording*. `setActiveRun` clears the flag so a stale one (left by a Force-Stop, which never reaches `clearActiveRun`) cannot make the next run start paused. If the source cannot be re-acquired on Resume — permission revoked, Bluetooth switched off — the run stays paused and the notification says so rather than being discarded, since the run is the user's and the obstacle is usually temporary. `gpsEnabled` is re-read on Resume because registering a `LocationListener` does not report the provider's current state and `onProviderDisabled` only fires on a change.

Because a cold pause makes the live stats go quiet, the notification grew Pause/Resume actions — it is the only affordance left after a reboot, where the run comes back paused and the app may never be opened. The queued-callback guards in `onSourceEnabled`/`onSatelliteStatus` stop an in-flight post from repainting the paused notification after the source is gone.

**Bluetooth reconnects back off, with `ACTION_ACL_CONNECTED` as a fast path.**
A dropped link retried every 3 s forever, so a receiver switched off or left behind woke the radio every 3 s for the rest of the run — the external-source twin of the pause problem. Retries now back off 3 s → 60 s, reset on a successful connect, with the reader thread parked on a `CountDownLatch` rather than spinning. Backing off alone would mean up to 60 s of lost logging, so the source also registers for `ACTION_ACL_CONNECTED` filtered to the paired address and counts the latch down the moment the device is really back. The broadcast is deliberately only a fast path, not the mechanism: whether a given receiver re-initiates the link on its own is device-dependent (unknown for the GNS 3000 until observed), and the backoff covers the case where it never does, so behaviour does not depend on the model in use. `BLUETOOTH_CONNECT` already covers receiving the broadcast, and no discovery is involved.

## Core Features

- **GPS logging foreground service** — records raw fixes at the chipset rate, survives Doze, resumes after process kill or reboot. Pause releases the receiver entirely, so a paused run costs no battery, and it stays paused across a restart.
- **Selectable recording source** — the internal GPS or a paired external classic-Bluetooth GNSS receiver (SPP/NMEA), chosen on the Settings tab.
- **Three destinations plus an Export page** — Record (status hero, start/stop/pause, live tiles while recording, the latest run while idle), Runs (tap to export, long-press to select; Delete with confirmation, Merge, Export on the selection) and Settings (inline GPS-device picker, debug log, updater); the Export page opens for the chosen runs with the filters and the live preview, and the notification offers Pause/Resume and Stop.
- **GPX export** — selected runs shared via the system share sheet from the Export tab, which carries the persisted accuracy/distance/time filters and a live preview of the filtered result (tracks, remaining points, percentage reduction).
- **In-app updater** — checks the GitHub `dev` pre-release and installs a newer signed nightly APK via the system package installer.
- **Debug NMEA log** — an optional Settings toggle tees the raw NMEA from a run to a timestamped text file, shareable from Settings, for diagnosing the receiver's constellations, rate and HDOP. For the internal GPS it also captures the chipset model, hardware year and GNSS capabilities (via `addNmeaListener` and the `getGnss*` probes).
